alt: Two panels. Left: the project's 14 packages as tiles; two are marked in red, search (12 points, scored 0) and cli, the command-line program (10 points, scored 0), because the checker places their hidden tests where they cannot compile. Right: bars, out of 100, for one complete, correct solution: 73.99 with the original checker and 94.70 with the fixed checker, a gain of 20.71 (search +11.29, cli +9.32, a skipped test +0.10).
caption: Hidden tests that cannot compile zero out 22 of 100 points for every solver who leaves the tests and package settings unchanged. The agent rebuilds a 14-package Rust project and is told not to edit the tests. The checker adds hidden tests to all 14 packages, and in two of them, search (12 points) and the command-line program (10 points), it places them where they do not compile, so both score 0. A complete, correct solution scores 73.99 out of 100 with the original checker as the publisher ran it and 94.70 with the fixed checker. The fixed checker places the hidden tests where they compile, and it also runs tests the original skipped after an earlier failure.
